entrypoints.summary: A client connected to an attacker-controlled NATS endpoint receives a MSG protocol line containing more than four whitespace-delimited arguments; the report's PoC serves this traffic with netcat to nats-publisher.

affected_components.role: MSG argument parser allocates a four-element stack descriptor array and writes descriptor fields while advancing index.

causal_paths.kind: network MSG arguments to stack descriptor writes

code_slices.fixed: No upstream patch or fixed code slice is present; the report recommends limiting writes to the array's actual size.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report identifies this as parsing of message arguments in cnats/src/parser.c and states that server-provided data with more than four arguments triggers the issue.
code_slices.vulnerable: _processMsgArgs declares struct slice slices[4], writes slices[index].start and slices[index].len during parsing, and increments index without a shown capacity check.

negative_controls: No fixed-version execution or negative-control run is present in the bundle.
observability.positive_marker: The report records 'stack smashing detected', process abort, and a core dump.

preconditions: A cnats-using application connects to an attacker-controlled or malicious NATS server endpoint.
The server can emit the protocol traffic consumed by the client parser.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A MSG line followed by five whitespace-delimited 'a' arguments and line termination.
trigger_steps.summary: Run the report's netcat listener, which sends INFO and PONG traffic followed by MSG with five repeated arguments; then point nats-publisher at that listener.

capabilities.concept: write beyond fixed stack slice descriptor array

mitigations.concept: bound parsed MSG arguments to slice-array capacity

relation_candidates.rationale: The report recommends limiting elements written to slices to the actual array size.

impact.affected_asset: Process integrity and availability of applications using the cnats client library; control-flow integrity is conditionally at risk on the stated build/architecture conditions.
impact.attacker_capability: A malicious NATS server endpoint can cause a connecting cnats client to parse an overlong MSG argument sequence and corrupt its stack.
impact.security_effect: Stack corruption causes observed process termination/denial of service; the report conditionally describes instruction-pointer overwrite and remote code execution on older compiler or 32-bit builds.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled server sends NATS protocol traffic whose MSG line contains more than four arguments.
_processMsgArgs reserves four stack slice descriptors but records parsed arguments using index without limiting index to the array capacity.

For each delimiter-terminated argument, and again for a final started argument, the parser writes slices[index].start and slices[index].len and increments index; excess arguments address elements beyond slices[4].

The report identifies a stack-based buffer overflow; its supplied execution terminates with stack-smashing detection and a core dump, while instruction-pointer overwrite and RCE are stated as possible on older compilers or 32-bit architectures.

failure.operation: Out-of-bounds stack writes through slices[index].start and slices[index].len in _processMsgArgs.

primary_invariant.statement: Every parsed MSG argument stored in slices must have an index within the four-element local slices array.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The parser increments index for parsed arguments without enforcing the four-element array limit before writing the start pointer and length.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report supplies source excerpt, a network PoC, and observed crash output. It does not supply historical upstream source, a remediation diff, affected/fixed version ranges, or a fixed-build regression result. RCE remains conditional report language rather than an end-to-end demonstrated payload.

remediation.invariant_restored: Limit elements written to slices to the actual four-element array capacity so no parsed argument maps outside the local descriptor array.
mitigation_classes: enforce parser argument-count bounds before slice writes
compiler hardening as defense in depth

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The client must connect to the attacker-controlled endpoint used by the netcat PoC, which emits protocol traffic including an overlong MSG argument sequence.
data_structure_invariants: The descriptor index must remain within slices capacity for every parser write.
Each parsed argument requires one slice descriptor.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report states index is incremented once per parsed argument and is not limited; attacker needs more than four MSG arguments.
numeric_domains.name: index

state_context.state_machine: The parser scans the received MSG argument buffer, accumulates token start/length state, stores a descriptor at argument boundaries, and finally stores a remaining started argument.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Cure53 report dated 2018-11-28; no affected release range is supplied

oracle.expected_negative: A parser implementation enforcing the slice-array capacity must not write beyond the four descriptor slots when processing excess MSG arguments; no execution result for a fixed build is supplied.
oracle.expected_positive: With a netcat server sending the report's MSG line containing five repeated arguments, nats-publisher terminates with a stack-smashing-detected message and core dump as reported.
